plan.summary: This 4-week block starts the 12-week off-camp build for boxing with one short full-body session each week. Week 1 establishes a simple strength baseline with a push-up assessment so future work can be progressed cleanly, and the main training starts in Week 2. With bodyweight-only equipment, the focus is crisp power first, then basic strength, then trunk work, while keeping fatigue low enough to fit around boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general strength and basic explosive ability with simple bodyweight movements that are easy to recover from alongside boxing.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the same patterns with slightly harder variations and tighter quality standards while keeping volume recoverable.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength in place and express it with faster, sharper bodyweight power work that supports boxing speed.

exercises.name: 1a. Squat Jump
exercises.notes: Land softly and reset between reps. Jump fast and high without letting the reps turn sloppy.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if squat jumps feel awkward. Same intent: fast takeoff, soft landing, full reset.

exercises.name: 1b. Plyo Push-Up to Hands-Elevated Surface
exercises.notes: Use a bench, box, or sturdy step height that lets you leave the surface slightly and land cleanly. Keep the reps quick and crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Fast Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you cannot leave the surface cleanly yet. Drive up as fast as possible and control the return.

exercises.name: 2. Push-Up
exercises.reps: AMRAP stopping 1 rep before form breaks
exercises.notes: This set establishes your starting strength level. Use a clean straight body line, chest close to the floor, and stop before the hips sag or range shortens.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up with a few easy sets, then do one hard max-rep set while stopping just before form breaks. Log the reps so the app can use this as your starting strength baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean push-up set and only count reps with full range and solid body position.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor push-ups are not yet clean. Pick a height that allows strong full-range reps.

exercises.name: 3. Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a controlled lower and stand up hard. Keep the front foot flat and the torso tall.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squats are uncomfortable to set up. Keep the reps smooth and balanced.

exercises.name: 4. Side Plank
exercises.notes: Keep a straight line from shoulder to ankle and do not let the hips roll back.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if side planks are too unstable right now. Keep the ribs down and squeeze glutes.

exercises.name: 1a. Squat Jump
exercises.notes: Each rep should look the same. Stop the set if jump height drops clearly.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it feels more natural. Keep the landing quiet and balanced.

exercises.name: 1b. Fast Incline Push-Up
exercises.notes: Drive up explosively and lower under control. Use a height that keeps every rep fast.

substitutionOptions.name: Plyo Push-Up to Hands-Elevated Surface
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you can leave the surface cleanly without losing shape.

exercises.name: 2. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave 1-2 clean reps in reserve on every set. If floor reps are too hard, elevate the hands and stay in the same rep range.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the strongest clean set in the target range and improve reps before making the variation harder.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a stable surface and keep the same rep target with clean full range.

exercises.name: 3. Split Squat
exercises.notes: Pause briefly at the bottom, then stand up with intent. Keep balance and knee tracking clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: A good swap if space or balance is limited.

exercises.name: 4. Bear Crawl Hold
exercises.notes: Hover knees just off the floor, push the ground away, and breathe quietly while staying braced.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the bear position bothers wrists or feels too unstable.

exercises.name: 1a. Squat Jump
exercises.notes: Jump with full intent but keep every landing soft and organized. Reset between reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it helps you move faster and cleaner.

exercises.name: 1b. Fast Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use the fastest variation you can perform cleanly. If speed slows down, stop the set.

substitutionOptions.name: Fast Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Best option if floor speed drops or technique breaks.

substitutionOptions.name: Plyo Push-Up to Hands-Elevated Surface
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you can leave the surface slightly and land under control.

exercises.name: 2. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Stay one rep shy of form breakdown. If all sets reach 10 clean reps, progress next block by lowering the hand elevation or using a harder variation.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean work set and aim to own the top of the rep range before progressing.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Keep the body straight and use a lower surface than last week if you are ready.

exercises.name: 3. Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Step back under control and push firmly through the front foot. Keep the torso steady.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if lunges bother your balance or knees.

exercises.name: 4. Side Plank
exercises.notes: Stay long through the body and keep the top shoulder stacked over the bottom shoulder.

substitutionOptions.name: Bear Crawl Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simpler trunk brace variation.

exercises.name: 1a. Squat Jump
exercises.notes: Deload week. Keep the jumps snappy and stop well before fatigue.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it feels fresher and easier to repeat cleanly.

exercises.name: 1b. Fast Incline Push-Up
exercises.notes: Move fast with clean mechanics. This week is about freshness, not chasing fatigue.

substitutionOptions.name: Fast Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if every rep stays quick and sharp.

exercises.name: 2. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use the same variation as last week but stop comfortably short of fatigue. Clean reps only.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the easiest strong set this week and use it to judge readiness going into the next block.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor reps feel grindy or slow this week.

exercises.name: 3. Split Squat
exercises.notes: Smooth reps, full control, no burn chasing. Save your legs for boxing work.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it feels more natural and easier to perform well.

exercises.name: 4. Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace lightly, breathe normally, and finish feeling better than when you started.

substitutionOptions.name: Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you prefer the lateral trunk challenge.
